title: AGENTS.md
text: Every network builder follows exact sequence: build_bipartite(data, field) — converts list-column sparse works × entities dgCMatrix. Normalizes entity labels toupper(trimws(...)). Calls ensure_list_column() first semicolon strings auto-split. apply_counting(B, counting, network_type) — weights binary matrix using one 13 counting methods (R/counting.R). Position-dependent methods (harmonic, arithmetic, geometric, etc.) use build_author_bipartite() instead generic path. multiply_bipartite(B, mode, similarity, threshold, top_n) — computes crossprod(B) (columns mode) tcrossprod(B) (rows mode) entirely sparse representation, optionally normalizes normalize() (R/normalize.R). Extracts upper-triangle edges without ever creating dense matrix. as_bibnets_network(edges, ..., format) R/methods.R — sole output format dispatcher. Stamps result bibnets_network S3 class (edgelist default), converts Gephi CSV, igraph, cograph, sparse matrix. Adding new output format requires editing one function.

title: Parsing and normalising author names
text: Bibliometric exports use three incompatible conventions. parse_names() recognises three; rule decided per string. comma always means Last, First. comma-less strings surname_first argument controls interpretation: "auto" (default) — surname-first iff trailing token looks like initials (-uppercase, 1–3 letters). bibnets-takes-precedence bias: native bibnets/Scopus labels parse correctly extra arguments, ordinary mixed-case "First Last" never misread. "yes" / TRUE — force surname-first. "" / FALSE — force given-first (comma-less returned unchanged). Particles suffixes handled, detection case-insensitive works bibnets’ upper-cased labels: Group / corporate authors, NA, empty strings left untouched:
code: parse_names(c("Saqr, Mohammed", "WANG Y", "Mohammed Saqr")) #> [1] "Mohammed Saqr" "Y WANG"        "Mohammed Saqr" #> attr(,"parts") #>         original    first last particle suffix   type #> 1 Saqr, Mohammed Mohammed Saqr     <NA>   <NA> person #> 2         WANG Y        Y WANG     <NA>   <NA> person #> 3  Mohammed Saqr Mohammed Saqr     <NA>   <NA> person parse_names("Wang Yong", surname_first = "yes")   # force surname-first #> [1] "Yong Wang" #> attr(,"parts") #>    original first last particle suffix   type #> 1 Wang Yong  Yong Wang     <NA>   <NA> person parse_names("WANG Y",    surname_first = "no")    # force given-first #> [1] "WANG Y" #> attr(,"parts") #>   original first last particle suffix   type #> 1   WANG Y  WANG    Y     <NA>   <NA> person parse_names(c("van der Berg, Jan", "Smith, John, Jr.",               "DE LA CRUZ, ANA", "VAN DER BERG J")) #> [1] "Jan van der Berg" "John Smith Jr"    "ANA DE LA CRUZ"   "J VAN DER BERG"   #> attr(,"parts") #>            original first  last particle suffix   type #> 1 van der Berg, Jan   Jan  Berg  van der   <NA> person #> 2  Smith, John, Jr.  John Smith     <NA>     Jr person #> 3   DE LA CRUZ, ANA   ANA  CRUZ    DE LA   <NA> person #> 4    VAN DER BERG J     J  BERG  VAN DER   <NA> person parse_names(c("WHO Collaborating Group", NA, "")) #> [1] "WHO Collaborating Group" NA                        #> [3] ""                        #> attr(,"parts") #>                  original first last particle suffix         type #> 1 WHO Collaborating Group  <NA> <NA>     <NA>   <NA> organization #> 2                    <NA>  <NA> <NA>     <NA>   <NA>      missing #> 3                          <NA> <NA>     <NA>   <NA>        empty

title: Extract network backbone using the disparity filter — backbone
text: null model asks: given node \(\) total strength \(s_i\) distributed uniformly across \(k_i\) edges, probability single edge weight large \(w_{ij}\)? answer $$\alpha_{ij} = \left(1 - \frac{w_{ij}}{s_i}\right)^{k_i - 1}$$ edge retained \(\min(\alpha_{ij}, \alpha_{ji}) < \alpha\). Nodes one edge always \(\alpha = 0\) always kept.

(Reference strings often contain internal commas, separate.) strip_quotes — every builder gains strip_quotes argument (default TRUE) removes surrounding quote characters (straight ", doubled "", curly quotes) entity, quoted CSV value like "Alice" ""Alice"" treated Alice.
